name: Sabine Ito
life: “I still remember learning that silence can be a paid part of a journey.” Monday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Sabine watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I drove the widow here and never asked why the box stayed in her lap. She told me on the way back.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and one cuff folded back twice. Sabine has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Sabine leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Sabine is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To collect the widow after an unhurried visit.
family: Alec Nielsen is Sabine’s cousin. Sabine makes the call. Alec is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The savings club*, Alec says, “I want the ticket home before my father forgets the songs we sing together.”
connections: Daria Singh. The widow can visit the shop with both handles present.

reactions.response: Sabine lets the widow hear the price privately and keep the box in hand.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Sabine stays where both neighbors can hear a familiar voice and gets news from the caretaker.
